metadata.subject: DBMS
metadata.title: Filter with SQL SELECT
metadata.description: Build a structured SELECT query, predict its matching rows, and inspect the computed result.

learning_objectives: Choose a source table with FROM.
Use WHERE to decide which rows survive.
Use SELECT to decide which columns appear.
Predict and explain the result of a bounded query.

mission.title: Build and test a SELECT query
mission.description: Choose FROM, SELECT, and WHERE, predict the matching rows, then run the real evaluator.

introduction.title: Ask a table for only the data you need
introduction.content: A table can contain many rows and columns. FROM chooses the table, WHERE keeps matching rows, and SELECT chooses the columns shown in the result.
points: A valid query can return many rows, one row, or no rows.
In this lesson, result order is not part of the question.

worked_example.title: Show names for ages 20 and above
worked_example.content: Start with a Students table containing Ana (19), Ben (22), and Cara (20).

steps.explanation: FROM students chooses the source table.
WHERE checks every source row against the condition.
SELECT keeps only the requested column after filtering.

worked_example.conclusion: The evaluator—not a memorized answer—calculates which rows and columns appear.

next.title: Now build it yourself.
next.content: Predict the matching rows before you run the query.

action_explanations.choose-source: FROM now identifies the table your query will read.
action_explanations.choose-columns: SELECT now identifies the columns the result will display.
action_explanations.build-where: WHERE will test this condition against every source row.
action_explanations.predict: Your prediction is saved. Run the query to compare it with the evaluator.
action_explanations.run-query: WHERE filtered the rows first; SELECT then projected the requested columns.

goal.instruction: Show the names of students aged 20 or older.
Show name and course for students whose course is CS.

source.title: Choose the source table
source.instruction: Which table contains the rows described by the goal?

columns.title: Choose the output columns
columns.instruction: Select only the columns the result should display.

where.title: Build the WHERE condition
where.instruction: Choose a field, operator, and value that keep the requested rows.

prediction.title: Predict the matching rows
prediction.instruction: Do not run yet. Select the source-row IDs you expect WHERE to keep.

run.title: Run and inspect the query
run.instruction: Execute your structured query and compare its real result with your prediction.

messages.missing_source: Choose a FROM table before running the query.
messages.missing_columns: Choose at least one SELECT column before running the query.
messages.missing_where: Complete the WHERE field, operator, and value before running the query.
messages.missing_prediction: Make an explicit prediction, including ‘No rows’, before running the query.
messages.success: Your query and prediction match the goal.
messages.prediction_mismatch: The query matches the goal, but the predicted rows differ from its computed result.
messages.valid_difference: That is a valid query and this is its real result, but it does not match the requested query goal.

visualization.prediction_instruction: Choose row IDs, or explicitly choose ‘No rows will match’.

actions.label: Choose the source table
actions.task: Choose the table named by the goal.

actions.label: Choose result columns
actions.task: Choose which columns SELECT should display.

actions.label: Run the query
actions.task: Run the evaluator and inspect the consequence.

challenge.title: Independent SELECT challenge
challenge.start_message: Build a second query without step-by-step button instructions.
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. Keep experimenting with valid queries.

phases.title: Build, predict, and run
phases.instruction: Use the goal and schema to construct the query, then predict its matching rows.

target.label: HIDDEN QUERY RESULT
target.description: The evaluator computes the result after RUN QUERY.

phases.feedback: Inspect which query field or predicted row differs from the goal.

guidance.start_message: Use the goal to build a small equality query and predict its rows.

items.content: Read the goal in FROM → WHERE → SELECT order, then predict source-row IDs.

phases.title: Practice SELECT
phases.instruction: Build the requested equality query and predict the result.
phases.feedback: Run a valid query and compare each field with the goal.

guidance.start_message: Apply a comparison operator with less guidance.

phases.title: Apply comparisons
phases.instruction: Construct and predict a comparison query.
phases.feedback: Check the boundary: > and >=, or < and <=, do not mean the same thing.

guidance.start_message: Independently choose among multiple fields, operators, and output columns.

phases.title: Solve the query
phases.instruction: Build the complete structured query and predict its result without hints.
phases.feedback: Your valid query shows a real consequence; revise only the fields that differ from the goal.

guidance.start_message: Handle randomized data, boundary values, and possibly an empty result.

phases.title: Master SELECT
phases.instruction: Derive the query and result from unfamiliar data.
phases.feedback: Re-evaluate the predicate row by row, including equality at the boundary.

quiz.question: In SELECT name FROM students WHERE age >= 20, which part decides which rows survive?

discovery.title: SELECT discovery
discovery.summary: WHERE filters source rows before SELECT projects the requested output columns.

sections.title: What?
sections.content: FROM chooses a table, WHERE filters rows, and SELECT projects columns.

sections.title: Example
sections.content: SELECT name FROM students WHERE age >= 20 asks for names only after testing each age.

sections.title: Why?
sections.content: Filtering first means columns not displayed by SELECT can still be used by WHERE.

sections.title: Remember
sections.content: FROM source → WHERE rows → SELECT columns.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of a spreadsheet filter
alternate_explanations.content: WHERE is like filtering rows in a spreadsheet; SELECT is like keeping only certain columns in the exported view.

alternate_explanations.title: Walk through one row
alternate_explanations.content: For age >= 20, test each age. Keep the row when the test is true, then copy only the selected fields into the result.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, how are WHERE and SELECT different?
recall.model_answer: WHERE decides which rows remain. SELECT decides which columns appear in the result.

thinking.title: Construct and predict the query
thinking.instruction: Use the unfamiliar table and goal. Enter a complete structured query and predict matching row IDs before checking.
thinking.do_not_execute: Do not reveal the result yet. Work through the predicate row by row.
thinking.empty_message: Complete every query field and enter matching row IDs or NONE.

feedback.all_correct: Your structured query and row prediction are correct.
feedback.incorrect: Review the field-level differences and recompute the matching rows.

solve.title: Expert SQL SELECT
solve.instruction: Construct the query and mentally predict its result with no hints.
